headline: Medium interaction risk: shared filesystem and write-capable ECC can feed Great Expectations inputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write files, use MCP, and treat session/skill files as workflow surfaces; Great Expectations reads data sources and validation results from files. That creates a plausible shared-file bridge where attacker-controlled content from one agent can influence the other. The pair is not directly documented interacting, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted directory
IF ECC ingests file content or MCP payloads as instructions
IF Great Expectations outputs are later parsed as directives by ECC
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable MCP paths that ingest untrusted files
Require manual review before copying outputs between agents
Prefix all inter-agent files with a non-executable schema header
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, while Great Expectations reads data sources and writes validation results. If they share a workspace, sensitive operational data can flow from ECC into GE outputs or logs. GE is network-egress none, which limits exfiltration, but the shared-file leakage path still exists in default-style local workflows.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same filesystem tree
IF ECC stores session summaries or security findings in shared paths
IF Great Expectations writes validation artifacts into that same tree
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions
Move sensitive ECC artifacts out of shared workspaces
Restrict GE output paths to a dedicated reports folder
Review validation outputs before publishing
requires-engineering: encrypt or redact shared artifacts automatically

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has filesystem write, git-state modification, subprocesses, and allowlisted network egress; Great Expectations can install packages and read/write validation artifacts. Overlap on the same mutable workspace can cause conflicting writes or package-state drift. Because both profiles show write-capable local operations, the conflict is plausible without extra assumptions.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same git repository
IF both write to overlapping output directories
IF package installation occurs in the same environment
mitigations: Assign separate git worktrees
Pin package versions before running either agent
Serialize runs with a simple lock file
Keep validation outputs in a dedicated directory
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate documentation, security findings, and session artifacts; Great Expectations can consume data sources and emit validation results. If GE treats ECC-produced artifacts as authoritative inputs, an error in ECC can cascade into incorrect validation or downstream decisions. The pairwise interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes artifacts produced by ECC
IF no human or automated verification step checks ECC outputs
IF downstream actions rely on GE validation results
mitigations: Require a second reviewer for ECC-generated artifacts
Add checksum or schema validation before GE ingestion
Keep ECC outputs read-only until approved
Annotate provenance on all handoff files
requires-engineering: enforce typed interfaces between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session summaries, hooks, and security findings, while Great Expectations handles data sources and validation results. No residency or certification mismatch is documented in either profile, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: shared handling of potentially sensitive operational data could create policy mismatch if the same data class is routed through both. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ECC session artifacts
IF Great Expectations stores validation results longer than the policy allows
IF the same dataset is routed through both agents without a retention review
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to either agent
Set short retention on shared artifacts
Avoid placing regulated data in session summaries
Document which outputs may be retained
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
